result: Accepted bounded-wait repair within the stated local scope.
reviewed: Full shared/memberSupport.ts helper and all14 new controlled component/SDK cases.
Caller lifetime is retired across digest, queue wait and storage awaits; late work cannot dispatch.
Underlying per-key operations stay serialized until actual settlement, including held setters and accepted cleanup.
Current-session acknowledgement updates UI once and starts ordered cleanup without retaining Send busy.
An identical later send remains safely queued and bounded; another payload is independent.
Session scope changes, exact UUID receipts and the atomic SQL boundary remain intact.
scopeLimits: Actual screens/wrappers/shared helper and installed SDK execute in a manual native hook/focus host with controlled Auth/storage/provider and virtual setTimeout. This is not an emulator or native-bridge scheduling proof.
The 32 browser cases use actual React/DOM/pages and synthetic Auth/provider/framework adapters. They preserve existing coverage; no deployed or provider acceptance is claimed.

The 15-second preparation budget is separate from the existing 12-second session lookup and 15-second write/readback deadlines; no single total 15-second latency claim. Confirmation cleanup has no UI wait, but its background storage operation can remain unresolved.

A stalled underlying storage operation intentionally continues to block only its own key. Later attempts fail visibly at their own preparation deadline; the queue is not released early because an uncancellable side effect could otherwise corrupt a newer identity.

Timeout/abort does not establish storage or server rollback. Stable UUID and exact database receipt validation remain required. No automatic write retry, SQL change, new migration invocation, provider write or branch/ref change occurred.
